predictions.title: Sub-7B open-weight reasoning models clear verified AIME-80 by Q1 2027
predictions.body: WeiboAI's VibeThinker-3B, a dense 3-billion-parameter MIT-licensed model built on Qwen2.5-3B, claims roughly 76 on AIME (into the 80s with test-time scaling) and about 80 Pass@1 on LiveCodeBench v6 using its Spectrum-to-Signal post-training pipeline, but those figures are self-reported and await reproduction. Set against the wider open-weight efficiency wave now landing weekly — GLM-5.2's fully-open MIT weights, vLLM v0.23.0 and SGLang v0.5.13 serving releases, and MosaicQuant 4-bit quantization — the trajectory points one way: post-training recipes, not parameter count, are closing the small-model reasoning gap. The prediction is that at least one open-weight model at or under 7 billion parameters will post an AIME score in the 80s that is corroborated on an independent third-party leaderboard or reproduction (not just the releasing team's own card), confirming that frontier verifiable-reasoning quality has moved into a size class that runs on a single consumer GPU or a high-end laptop.

reasoning.because: VibeThinker-3B (MIT, 3B) claims ~76 AIME rising into the 80s, on a model that runs almost anywhere
reasoning.given: Open-weight post-training and serving recipes (GLM-5.2, vLLM, SGLang, MosaicQuant) compound weekly
reasoning.so_that: An independent leaderboard or reproduction corroborates an 80s-AIME score from a model at or under 7B parameters
reasoning.landing: by Q1 2027; a third-party leaderboard verifies a sub-7B model at AIME-80
reasoning.plain_language: Tiny free AI models that fit on one computer are getting good enough at hard math that outsiders will confirm the scores.

predictions.summary: VibeThinker-3B claims AIME scores in the 80s for a 3B MIT-licensed model, but the numbers are self-reported. Amid a weekly cadence of open-weight and inference-efficiency releases, expect an independent leaderboard or reproduction to corroborate an 80s-AIME score from a sub-7B model by Q1 2027.

predictions.title: Google DeepMind unveils a senior-researcher retention package by Q4 2026
predictions.body: The same-week exits of Nobel laureate John Jumper to Anthropic and Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer to OpenAI mark an acceleration of senior research talent leaving Google, and the financial backdrop shows why poaching is affordable for rivals: OpenAI tripled revenue year over year to 5.7 billion dollars in the first quarter and sits on more than 73 billion dollars in cash after its spring raise, ammunition that funds aggressive compensation. Google already paid a reported 2.7 billion dollars under two years ago to bring Shazeer's team back, so losing him plus a marquee AlphaFold name in a 48-hour window is the kind of reputational and capability loss that forces a structural response rather than one-off counteroffers. Expect Google or DeepMind leadership to roll out a named retention and compensation mechanism aimed at its most senior researchers ahead of the next Gemini cycle, whether framed as accelerated equity, multi-year founder-style grants, or expanded autonomy and compute guarantees for principal scientists.

reasoning.because: Jumper and Shazeer both exited Google in one 48-hour window for Anthropic and OpenAI respectively
reasoning.given: Cash-rich rivals can outbid, and Google already paid 2.7B to retain Shazeer once
reasoning.so_that: Google moves from ad hoc counteroffers to a structural senior-researcher retention program before its next Gemini launch
reasoning.landing: Google or DeepMind announces a named retention package by Q4 2026
reasoning.plain_language: Google's star AI scientists keep leaving for rivals, so Google will likely offer a big new deal to keep the rest.

predictions.summary: John Jumper left Google DeepMind for Anthropic and Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer left for OpenAI in one 48-hour window, leaving Google with a senior-talent exodus as cash-rich rivals outbid it. Expect Google or DeepMind to announce a structural retention package for senior researchers by Q4 2026.

predictions.title: Commerce issues frontier-model export-control framework by Q1 2027
predictions.body: The mid-June export-control freeze on Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 -- imposed on a case-by-case directive that named no published rule, took both models offline for all foreign persons, and rested on what the company describes as verbal evidence of a narrow jailbreak -- exposes the absence of any codified standard for when a frontier model's capabilities trigger export controls. With a bipartisan House group now demanding Commerce Secretary Lutnick document the legal basis and national-security rationale, and security researchers publicly disputing that ordinary defensive code-analysis should be controllable, the pressure is toward a written, generally-applicable framework rather than ad-hoc per-model orders. The prediction is that by Q1 2027 the Commerce Department (BIS) publishes a formal capability-threshold framework -- a proposed rule, interim final rule, or detailed guidance -- defining which model capabilities and evaluation triggers bring a frontier model under export-control jurisdiction, the way the Export Administration Regulations already gate advanced AI chips. The competitive consequence is durable: a published threshold tells every US lab which capabilities carry deployment-blocking risk, shifting near-term foreign-market access toward whichever frontier systems sit below the line.

reasoning.because: Fable 5 / Mythos 5 were frozen by a case-by-case directive citing no published capability rule
reasoning.given: bipartisan House oversight plus researcher pushback pressures a codified standard over ad-hoc orders
reasoning.so_that: Commerce publishes a capability-threshold framework defining when a frontier model falls under export control
reasoning.landing: Commerce/BIS publishes the framework by Q1 2027 as a rule or formal guidance
reasoning.plain_language: After regulators pulled two Anthropic models with no clear rule, lawmakers are pushing the government to write down exactly when an AI model gets export-blocked.

predictions.summary: Anthropic's Fable 5 and Mythos 5 were frozen with no published rule, prompting a bipartisan House demand that Commerce justify it. That pressure points toward Commerce publishing a framework by Q1 2027 defining when a frontier model's capabilities trigger export controls, like US chip rules.
